title: Name the relationship first
intro: Priya is editing her lab report the night before it's due. Every paragraph is missing one transition.
hook: Before you look at the choices, say how the two sentences connect: same direction, opposite, cause, example, or time.

steps.prompt: Priya's method. Put the steps in order.
items: Read the sentence before the blank
Name the relationship in one word
Pick the transition that matches it
steps.why: Both sentences first, then the relationship, then the choices. Reading choices first makes them all sound fine.

steps.prompt: Paragraph 1. Sort each transition by the relationship it signals.
steps.why: Knowing the family of a transition lets you eliminate choices that mean the same thing.

steps.prompt: Paragraph 2: 'We expected the seeds in the dark to fail. ______, they sprouted at the same rate as the others.'
steps.why: Expected to fail, then sprouted: the result went against expectations.

steps.prompt: Read fast. Then: which word is the odd one out?
steps.why: Consequently signals a result. All the others signal a contrast.

steps.prompt: Paragraph 3: 'The first trial used tap water. ______, the second trial used distilled water.'
steps.why: Two trials set side by side with a difference: contrast. Nothing causes anything here.

steps.prompt: If two answer choices mean the same thing, what does that tell you?
steps.answer: Neither can be right, because a question has only one correct answer. Eliminate both.

keys: Read both sentences, name the relationship, then pick.
Learn transition families: contrast, cause, addition, example, time.
Two choices from the same family cancel each other out.

recall.prompt: 'The trail was steep. ______, the hikers reached the top by noon.'
recall.why: Steep would slow them, yet they made it: contrast.

recall.prompt: What's the first step on a transition question?
recall.answer: Read the sentences on both sides and name how they relate, before looking at the choices.
